questions.prompt: Which statement best describes flexibility in sports and recreation?
options: The ability of a joint to move through a useful range of motion
The ability to hold the breath for a long period
The maximum speed reached during a sprint race
The number of officials assigned to a game
questions.correctAnswer: The ability of a joint to move through a useful range of motion
questions.explanation: Flexibility is the capacity of muscles and joints to allow movement through a safe range. It supports efficient and comfortable performance.
questions.learningOutcome: Define flexibility as a component of health and fitness in sport.

questions.prompt: Which activity is an example of a dynamic stretch before a football match?
options: Walking lunges across the field
Sitting still in a toe-touch position for one minute
Recording scores on a score sheet
Measuring body mass with a weighing scale
questions.correctAnswer: Walking lunges across the field
questions.explanation: Dynamic stretching uses controlled movement to prepare muscles and joints. Walking lunges warm the legs while moving through a range of motion.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify dynamic stretches used to prepare for physical activity.

questions.prompt: A sprinter holds a hamstring stretch after training without bouncing. Which type of stretch is being used?
options: Static stretch
Agility drill
Plyometric jump
Anaerobic sprint
questions.correctAnswer: Static stretch
questions.explanation: A static stretch is held in one position for a short period. It is often used after activity to help maintain flexibility.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish static stretching from other training activities.

questions.prompt: Why should learners avoid bouncing forcefully during a static stretch?
options: It can strain muscles and reduce safe control of movement
It always improves joint safety immediately
It changes a stretch into official scoring
It makes the heart stop adapting to exercise
questions.correctAnswer: It can strain muscles and reduce safe control of movement
questions.explanation: Forceful bouncing can overstretch tissues and increase injury risk. Controlled stretching is safer and easier to monitor.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safety principles when performing flexibility activities.

questions.prompt: Which sequence is most suitable for preparing the body before a netball training session?
options: Light jogging, dynamic stretches, then sport-specific movement drills
Static stretching only, then immediate high-speed play
Heavy strength lifts, then no warm-up activity
Eating a large meal, then sprinting without preparation
questions.correctAnswer: Light jogging, dynamic stretches, then sport-specific movement drills
questions.explanation: A progressive warm-up raises body temperature, mobilises joints, and prepares movement patterns. This reduces injury risk and improves readiness.
questions.learningOutcome: Select appropriate warm-up activities for sport participation.

questions.prompt: During peer assessment, which observation best shows good form in a calf stretch?
options: The back heel stays down while the movement is controlled
The learner twists the knee sharply inward
The learner holds the breath until the stretch ends
The front foot is lifted off the ground throughout
questions.correctAnswer: The back heel stays down while the movement is controlled
questions.explanation: Good stretching form keeps body alignment controlled and avoids sudden joint stress. The heel-down position helps stretch the calf safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Use observable criteria to assess safe stretching form.

questions.prompt: A basketball player is flexible but keeps losing balance during stretching drills. Which coaching feedback is most useful?
options: Reduce speed, widen the base of support, and control breathing
Stretch harder until pain becomes constant
Stop all flexibility work and only practise shooting
Close the eyes for every standing stretch
questions.correctAnswer: Reduce speed, widen the base of support, and control breathing
questions.explanation: Balance improves when the body has a stable base and controlled movement. Pain is not a safe target for flexibility training.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse performance problems during flexibility activities and recommend safe corrections.

questions.prompt: Which plan best develops flexibility for a school volleyball team over four weeks?
options: Use regular dynamic warm-ups, safe static cool-down stretches, and weekly range-of-motion checks
Stretch once at the end of the month and skip warm-ups
Use only maximal jumps because flexibility is unrelated to volleyball
Replace all practice sessions with written notes about stretching
questions.correctAnswer: Use regular dynamic warm-ups, safe static cool-down stretches, and weekly range-of-motion checks
questions.explanation: A useful flexibility plan is regular, progressive, safe, and measurable. Monitoring range of motion helps learners see improvement.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a simple flexibility improvement plan for a team sport.

questions.prompt: What is muscular strength?
options: The ability of a muscle or muscle group to produce force
The ability to remember game rules quickly
The ability to relax without physical movement
The ability to officiate without assistants
questions.correctAnswer: The ability of a muscle or muscle group to produce force
questions.explanation: Muscular strength is about force production. It helps athletes push, pull, lift, jump, and resist external loads.
questions.learningOutcome: Define muscular strength as a fitness component.

questions.prompt: Which activity mainly tests muscular endurance?
options: Performing many controlled press-ups without stopping
Lifting the heaviest possible weight once
Sleeping for eight hours after training
Reading a tournament fixture list
questions.correctAnswer: Performing many controlled press-ups without stopping
questions.explanation: Muscular endurance is the ability to repeat contractions or sustain effort over time. Many press-ups test repeated muscle work.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify activities that develop or test muscular endurance.

questions.prompt: Why is good form important when using improvised weights made from sand-filled bottles?
options: It helps muscles work safely and reduces injury risk
It makes the bottles heavier without adding sand
It removes the need for warm-up activities
It changes endurance into a ball game
questions.correctAnswer: It helps muscles work safely and reduces injury risk
questions.explanation: Improvised equipment can be useful, but safe body alignment and controlled movement are essential. Poor form can overload joints or muscles.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of safe form during strength and endurance activities.

questions.prompt: A learner wants stronger legs for long jump take-off. Which activity is most relevant?
options: Controlled squats with proper knee alignment
Only practising handwriting speed
Holding a whistle during practice
Avoiding all lower-body movement
questions.correctAnswer: Controlled squats with proper knee alignment
questions.explanation: Squats can strengthen major leg muscles used in take-off. Proper alignment helps the learner train safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply strength training choices to sport performance needs.

questions.prompt: Which instruction best supports safety during a plank endurance activity?
options: Keep the body aligned and stop if sharp pain occurs
Hold the breath until the timer ends
Let the lower back sag to make it easier
Compete to ignore all signs of discomfort
questions.correctAnswer: Keep the body aligned and stop if sharp pain occurs
questions.explanation: A plank should maintain a neutral body line and controlled breathing. Sharp pain is a warning sign that the activity should stop.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safety rules during body-weight endurance activities.

questions.prompt: A team can complete 20 sit-ups but struggles to hold good posture in the final repetitions. What is the best adjustment?
options: Reduce repetitions and rebuild quality before increasing volume
Add more repetitions even when form collapses
Remove all rest periods permanently
Use heavier equipment immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Reduce repetitions and rebuild quality before increasing volume
questions.explanation: Training should protect technique before increasing workload. Quality movement supports safe and effective progress.
questions.learningOutcome: Modify endurance activities based on observed performance quality.

questions.prompt: Which comparison between muscular strength and muscular endurance is most accurate?
options: Strength focuses on force, while endurance focuses on sustaining repeated muscle effort
Strength and endurance both mean only running fast
Endurance is unrelated to muscles
Strength is measured only by heart rate recovery
questions.correctAnswer: Strength focuses on force, while endurance focuses on sustaining repeated muscle effort
questions.explanation: Strength and endurance are related but different fitness components. Both can be trained with appropriate overload and recovery.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse differences between muscular strength and muscular endurance.

questions.prompt: Which mini-circuit best combines muscular strength, muscular endurance, and environmental responsibility?
options: Squats, press-ups, and safe lifts using clean recycled bottle weights
Only watching online videos about athletes
Repeated whistle blowing and score recording
Maximum lifting with unknown loads and no supervision
questions.correctAnswer: Squats, press-ups, and safe lifts using clean recycled bottle weights
questions.explanation: A useful circuit can use body weight and safely improvised equipment. Reusing clean materials also supports environmental responsibility.
questions.learningOutcome: Design a simple safe circuit for muscular fitness using locally available resources.

questions.prompt: What does cardiovascular endurance mainly describe?
options: The ability of the heart, lungs, and blood vessels to support sustained activity
The ability to memorise a referee signal
The amount of chalk used to mark a field
The number of players on a substitution bench
questions.correctAnswer: The ability of the heart, lungs, and blood vessels to support sustained activity
questions.explanation: Cardiovascular endurance supports continuous physical activity by delivering oxygen to working muscles. It is important in many games and sports.
questions.learningOutcome: Define cardiovascular endurance as a health-related fitness component.

questions.prompt: Which activity is best for improving cardiovascular endurance in a school setting?
options: Continuous moderate running or skipping for several minutes
Holding a stretch without movement for ten seconds
Lifting one heavy object once
Writing team names on a fixture chart
questions.correctAnswer: Continuous moderate running or skipping for several minutes
questions.explanation: Sustained rhythmic activity challenges the heart and lungs. Running and skipping can improve endurance when done progressively.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify exercises that develop cardiovascular endurance.

questions.prompt: Why does breathing rate usually increase during continuous running?
options: The body needs more oxygen and must remove more carbon dioxide
The bones stop supporting movement
The whistle signal becomes louder
The body no longer needs energy
questions.correctAnswer: The body needs more oxygen and must remove more carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: Working muscles need more oxygen to release energy. Faster breathing helps meet this demand and remove carbon dioxide.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain body responses during sustained physical activity.

questions.prompt: A learner becomes breathless too quickly during a 10-minute jog. Which first adjustment is most appropriate?
options: Slow to a sustainable pace and build duration gradually
Sprint harder until the learner collapses
Skip all warm-ups and try again
Stop drinking water during the whole day
questions.correctAnswer: Slow to a sustainable pace and build duration gradually
questions.explanation: Endurance improves through progressive overload at a manageable intensity. Training should be challenging but safe.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply pacing principles to endurance training.

questions.prompt: Which method can learners use to monitor exercise intensity during an endurance session?
options: Check pulse rate or use the talk test
Count the number of cones in storage
Compare shoe colours after training
Measure the length of a whistle cord
questions.correctAnswer: Check pulse rate or use the talk test
questions.explanation: Pulse rate and the talk test give practical clues about effort level. They help learners train within a safe intensity range.
questions.learningOutcome: Use simple measures to monitor cardiovascular training intensity.

questions.prompt: Which practice best reduces risk during high-impact aerobic activities?
options: Land softly with bent knees and use suitable footwear
Always land with locked knees
Train on slippery ground to build courage
Avoid cooling down after hard activity
questions.correctAnswer: Land softly with bent knees and use suitable footwear
questions.explanation: Soft landings reduce stress on joints. Suitable footwear and surfaces also help make aerobic training safer.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safety measures during aerobic endurance activities.

questions.prompt: A coach compares two learners after six weeks of jogging. Learner A has a lower resting pulse and recovers faster after exercise. What is the best interpretation?
options: Learner A likely improved cardiovascular fitness
Learner A must have lost all muscle strength
Learner A no longer needs warm-ups
Learner A cannot participate in team sports
questions.correctAnswer: Learner A likely improved cardiovascular fitness
questions.explanation: Faster recovery and a lower resting pulse can indicate improved heart and lung efficiency. Interpretation should still consider overall health and training context.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse simple fitness indicators after endurance training.

questions.prompt: Which weekly plan best improves cardiovascular endurance for beginners while allowing recovery?
options: Three moderate sessions with warm-up, main activity, cool-down, and rest days between some sessions
One very hard session every month with no preparation
Daily maximum sprinting without rest
Only stretching the arms for two minutes each week
questions.correctAnswer: Three moderate sessions with warm-up, main activity, cool-down, and rest days between some sessions
questions.explanation: Endurance development needs regular practice and recovery. A planned weekly routine reduces overload and supports steady adaptation.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a basic cardiovascular endurance plan for beginner learners.

questions.prompt: What is posture in relation to sport performance?
options: The alignment and positioning of body parts during rest or movement
The number of medals won by a school team
The official size of a playing field
The length of a training timetable
questions.correctAnswer: The alignment and positioning of body parts during rest or movement
questions.explanation: Posture describes how the body is aligned. Efficient posture supports balance, force production, and movement control.
questions.learningOutcome: Define posture as body alignment during sport and recreation.

questions.prompt: Which example shows efficient posture when landing from a jump?
options: Knees bent, trunk controlled, and feet landing under the body
Knees locked and body leaning far backward
Head turned away with eyes closed
One foot landing on another learner's shoe
questions.correctAnswer: Knees bent, trunk controlled, and feet landing under the body
questions.explanation: Controlled landing posture helps absorb force safely. It also improves balance for the next movement.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise efficient posture during basic sport movements.

questions.prompt: Why does poor posture during repeated lifting increase injury risk?
options: It can place unnecessary stress on muscles, joints, and the spine
It makes equipment lighter than expected
It prevents all muscle activity
It changes a training drill into a rest period
questions.correctAnswer: It can place unnecessary stress on muscles, joints, and the spine
questions.explanation: Poor alignment can overload body structures. Proper lifting posture spreads force more safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how posture affects safety during physical activity.

questions.prompt: A learner bends from the waist with rounded back to pick up a medicine ball. What correction is best?
options: Bend the knees, keep the back neutral, and hold the load close
Twist quickly while lifting
Lock the knees and pull with the neck
Lift the ball far away from the body
questions.correctAnswer: Bend the knees, keep the back neutral, and hold the load close
questions.explanation: Safe lifting uses the legs and keeps the load close to reduce strain. A neutral back supports better control.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply posture corrections during safe lifting tasks.

questions.prompt: Which cue best helps a runner maintain efficient posture during a middle-distance race?
options: Run tall, keep shoulders relaxed, and look ahead
Clench fists tightly and look at the ground throughout
Lean backward and swing arms across the body
Hold the breath on every bend
questions.correctAnswer: Run tall, keep shoulders relaxed, and look ahead
questions.explanation: A tall relaxed posture supports breathing and efficient running mechanics. Looking ahead also helps balance and direction.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply posture cues to improve running performance.

questions.prompt: A volleyball player often bends the back instead of the knees when receiving low balls. Which drill is most useful?
options: Repeated ready-position practice with knees flexed and chest lifted
More serving practice with no receiving work
Writing definitions of posture only
Standing still with locked knees during every drill
questions.correctAnswer: Repeated ready-position practice with knees flexed and chest lifted
questions.explanation: The ready position trains efficient body alignment for quick movement. Repetition helps the learner apply posture in game situations.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose drills that correct posture problems in sport skills.

questions.prompt: Which observation best explains why a hurdler clips barriers late in a race?
options: Fatigue may reduce posture control and leg clearance
Good posture always causes more hurdle contact
Hydration has no link to performance
Officials caused the hurdler's hip position
questions.correctAnswer: Fatigue may reduce posture control and leg clearance
questions.explanation: Fatigue can affect trunk control, stride mechanics, and leg action. Analysing posture late in performance helps identify technique breakdown.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how fatigue can affect posture and performance technique.

questions.prompt: Which checklist would best help peers assess posture during a squat exercise?
options: Back neutral, knees tracking over toes, heels grounded, and movement controlled
Shoe colour, shirt number, field size, and whistle tone
Number of spectators, weather, and team nickname
Ability to talk loudly while ignoring alignment
questions.correctAnswer: Back neutral, knees tracking over toes, heels grounded, and movement controlled
questions.explanation: A posture checklist should focus on observable body alignment and control. These criteria help peers give useful feedback.
questions.learningOutcome: Create criteria for peer assessment of posture in fitness activities.

questions.prompt: What is recreation in the context of wellness?
options: Voluntary activities done for enjoyment, relaxation, and health
Only professional competition for prize money
A medical treatment that replaces all exercise
A rule book used only by referees
questions.correctAnswer: Voluntary activities done for enjoyment, relaxation, and health
questions.explanation: Recreation includes chosen leisure activities that support physical, mental, and social well-being. It can be active or less physically demanding.
questions.learningOutcome: Define recreation and relate it to wellness.

questions.prompt: Which activity best shows active recreation that can promote wellness?
options: A weekend community walk in a safe park
Sitting indoors all day with no movement
Skipping sleep to watch sport highlights
Eating snacks while avoiding all activity
questions.correctAnswer: A weekend community walk in a safe park
questions.explanation: Active recreation uses enjoyable movement to support health. Walking can improve fitness, mood, and social connection.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify recreational activities that support wellness.

questions.prompt: How can recreational sports help mental wellness for Grade 10 learners?
options: They can reduce stress, improve mood, and build social support
They guarantee that learners never feel tired
They remove the need for studying
They prevent all injuries without safety planning
questions.correctAnswer: They can reduce stress, improve mood, and build social support
questions.explanation: Recreational sport can support emotional balance and friendship. It should be planned safely and balanced with other responsibilities.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain links between recreation, mental wellness, and social well-being.

questions.prompt: A school wants a wellness activity that includes learners with different fitness levels. Which choice is best?
options: A station-based fun circuit with adjustable intensity at each station
A compulsory maximum sprint contest for every learner
A single elimination event where beginners stop immediately
A drill that allows only the fastest learners to participate
questions.correctAnswer: A station-based fun circuit with adjustable intensity at each station
questions.explanation: Inclusive recreation allows learners to participate at suitable levels. Adjustable intensity supports safety, enjoyment, and confidence.
questions.learningOutcome: Select inclusive recreational activities for mixed-ability groups.

questions.prompt: Which action best supports environmental conservation during an outdoor recreation trip?
options: Carry back litter and use marked paths to protect vegetation
Leave plastic bottles at the picnic site
Cut tree branches to mark every route
Make new paths through fragile areas
questions.correctAnswer: Carry back litter and use marked paths to protect vegetation
questions.explanation: Responsible recreation protects natural spaces. Proper waste handling and path use reduce environmental damage.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply environmental responsibility during recreational activities.

questions.prompt: Which recreational programme best balances physical, social, and safety needs?
options: Warm-up, mixed-team games, hydration breaks, first-aid readiness, and reflection
Only competitive finals with no rest or first-aid plan
A timetable with no supervision or rules
Activities chosen only by the strongest learners
questions.correctAnswer: Warm-up, mixed-team games, hydration breaks, first-aid readiness, and reflection
questions.explanation: A good programme plans movement, inclusion, safety, and learning. Reflection helps learners connect activity to wellness.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan safe recreational sessions that promote wellness.

questions.prompt: A learner says recreation is a waste of study time. Which response best evaluates this view?
options: Balanced recreation can support health, concentration, and social skills when time is managed well
Recreation should replace all schoolwork
Only elite athletes benefit from recreation
Wellness has no connection to learning
questions.correctAnswer: Balanced recreation can support health, concentration, and social skills when time is managed well
questions.explanation: Recreation is valuable when balanced with learning and rest. Wellness can improve readiness to learn and participate.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse the role of recreation in balanced learner wellness.

questions.prompt: Which proposal best creates a school recreation club that supports wellness?
options: Offer varied activities, inclusive rules, safety checks, learner leadership, and regular review
Hold one activity for only expert players and ignore feedback
Ban warm-ups to save time
Choose activities without considering space, equipment, or safety
questions.correctAnswer: Offer varied activities, inclusive rules, safety checks, learner leadership, and regular review
questions.explanation: A strong recreation club is organised, inclusive, safe, and responsive to learners. Review helps improve participation and wellness outcomes.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a recreation club plan that promotes wellness and inclusion.

questions.prompt: Which injury is most likely described as a sprain?
options: An injury to a ligament around a joint
A complete improvement in flexibility
A planned rest day after training
A referee's signal for substitution
questions.correctAnswer: An injury to a ligament around a joint
questions.explanation: A sprain affects ligaments, which connect bones at joints. Ankles are common sites for sprains in sport.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common types of sports injuries.

questions.prompt: Which situation is a common cause of acute sports injury?
options: A sudden collision or awkward landing during play
A balanced meal before training
A planned cool-down after exercise
Checking equipment before a match
questions.correctAnswer: A sudden collision or awkward landing during play
questions.explanation: Acute injuries happen suddenly during activity. Collisions and awkward landings can damage muscles, ligaments, or bones.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise causes of common sports injuries.

questions.prompt: Why should damaged playing surfaces be reported before a game starts?
options: They can increase the chance of falls, twists, and collisions
They automatically improve player speed
They make first aid unnecessary
They remove the need for officials
questions.correctAnswer: They can increase the chance of falls, twists, and collisions
questions.explanation: Unsafe surfaces are a preventable risk. Reporting hazards allows organisers to repair, mark, or avoid dangerous areas.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain environmental risk factors for sports injuries.

questions.prompt: A learner twists an ankle and cannot continue playing. What should teammates do first?
options: Stop play, keep the learner safe, and call the teacher or first-aider
Force the learner to finish the game
Massage the injury strongly without checking
Leave the learner alone and continue training
questions.correctAnswer: Stop play, keep the learner safe, and call the teacher or first-aider
questions.explanation: Immediate safety and adult or trained first-aid support come first. Continuing to play can worsen an injury.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply immediate safety steps when a sports injury occurs.

questions.prompt: Which strategy best helps prevent overuse injuries in training?
options: Increase workload gradually and include recovery periods
Repeat hard training daily without rest
Ignore pain until competition ends
Change footwear only when an injury occurs
questions.correctAnswer: Increase workload gradually and include recovery periods
questions.explanation: Overuse injuries often result from repeated stress without enough recovery. Gradual progression helps tissues adapt.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply training-load principles to reduce overuse injury risk.

questions.prompt: Which item is most important to check before a school hockey practice to reduce injury risk?
options: Stick condition, shin guards, playing space, and safe rules
The colour of the scoreboard only
The number of spectators near the gate
The brand of the coach's notebook
questions.correctAnswer: Stick condition, shin guards, playing space, and safe rules
questions.explanation: Equipment, protective gear, space, and rules all affect safety. Checking them before practice prevents avoidable harm.
questions.learningOutcome: Use pre-activity checks to reduce injury risk in sport.

questions.prompt: An athlete keeps training through shin pain that worsens each week. Which analysis is most appropriate?
options: The pattern suggests a possible overuse problem that needs rest and assessment
The athlete is definitely becoming fitter because pain always means progress
The pain proves warm-ups are unnecessary
The athlete should double the running distance immediately
questions.correctAnswer: The pattern suggests a possible overuse problem that needs rest and assessment
questions.explanation: Worsening repeated pain is a warning sign. Rest, load review, and qualified assessment help prevent a more serious injury.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse warning signs of overuse injury in sport.

questions.prompt: Which school injury-prevention policy would be most complete for inter-house games?
options: Risk assessment, warm-up routines, equipment checks, first-aid plan, and incident reporting
Only a trophy display and team songs
No water breaks so games end quickly
Players decide all safety rules during play
questions.correctAnswer: Risk assessment, warm-up routines, equipment checks, first-aid plan, and incident reporting
questions.explanation: A complete policy prevents injuries and prepares staff to respond if they occur. It also records incidents for future improvement.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a basic safety policy for school sports activities.

questions.prompt: Which role best describes a sports coach?
options: A person who guides athletes to learn skills, train safely, and improve performance
A person who only sells equipment to teams
A person who ignores rules during matches
A person who replaces all officials in every sport
questions.correctAnswer: A person who guides athletes to learn skills, train safely, and improve performance
questions.explanation: Coaches plan learning experiences, teach skills, support motivation, and protect safety. They help athletes grow over time.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the role of a coach in sports and recreation.

questions.prompt: Which quality is most important for a beginner coach working with school learners?
options: Clear communication and respect for learner safety
Favouring only the most talented player
Avoiding feedback during practice
Changing rules randomly to confuse learners
questions.correctAnswer: Clear communication and respect for learner safety
questions.explanation: Coaching depends on clear instructions and a safe learning environment. Fairness and respect help learners participate confidently.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify qualities of effective beginner coaching.

questions.prompt: Why should a coach set clear objectives before a training session?
options: Objectives guide activities, feedback, and assessment of progress
Objectives make equipment checks unnecessary
Objectives guarantee victory in every match
Objectives remove the need to observe learners
questions.correctAnswer: Objectives guide activities, feedback, and assessment of progress
questions.explanation: Clear objectives help the coach choose suitable drills and measure learning. They also keep the session focused.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose of objectives in coaching sessions.

questions.prompt: A coach wants to teach passing in handball to beginners. Which approach is most suitable?
options: Demonstrate the pass, allow guided practice, observe, and give simple feedback
Start with a full-speed match and ignore mistakes
Only lecture about handball history
Punish every error before learners practise
questions.correctAnswer: Demonstrate the pass, allow guided practice, observe, and give simple feedback
questions.explanation: Beginners benefit from demonstration, practice, observation, and feedback. This sequence supports skill learning and confidence.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply basic coaching steps when teaching a new skill.

questions.prompt: Which feedback is most useful after a learner misses a chest pass target?
options: Step toward the target and extend both arms as you release the ball
You are bad at passing
Never try passing again
The target should move closer without you changing technique
questions.correctAnswer: Step toward the target and extend both arms as you release the ball
questions.explanation: Useful feedback is specific and connected to performance cues. It tells the learner what to improve next.
questions.learningOutcome: Give constructive feedback to improve sport skills.

questions.prompt: Which coaching decision best supports fair participation during a mixed-ability class game?
options: Rotate roles and adapt rules so all learners practise the target skill
Let only strong players touch the ball
Remove learners who are still learning
Ignore beginners so advanced players finish quickly
questions.correctAnswer: Rotate roles and adapt rules so all learners practise the target skill
questions.explanation: Inclusive coaching gives every learner meaningful practice. Modified rules can protect skill development and enjoyment.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply inclusive coaching strategies in class activities.

questions.prompt: A team improves fitness but keeps making poor decisions in game situations. What should the coach analyse?
options: Whether practice includes tactical decision-making under realistic pressure
Only the colour of training bibs
The number of balls stored in the office
Whether players know the school anthem
questions.correctAnswer: Whether practice includes tactical decision-making under realistic pressure
questions.explanation: Game performance needs decision-making as well as fitness. Training should include realistic situations that require choices.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse gaps between training content and game performance.

questions.prompt: Which session plan best shows effective coaching structure?
options: Objective, warm-up, skill demonstration, progressive practice, feedback, cool-down, and review
Random drills without objectives or feedback
A full match only with no safety checks
A lecture only with no learner practice
questions.correctAnswer: Objective, warm-up, skill demonstration, progressive practice, feedback, cool-down, and review
questions.explanation: An organised session links goals, safety, practice, feedback, and reflection. This helps learners improve and understand their progress.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a structured beginner coaching session plan.

questions.prompt: What does improvisation of sports equipment mean?
options: Creating or adapting equipment using available safe materials
Buying the most expensive imported equipment only
Using damaged equipment without checking it
Cancelling all practice when standard equipment is missing
questions.correctAnswer: Creating or adapting equipment using available safe materials
questions.explanation: Improvisation helps learners participate when standard resources are limited. Safety and suitability must guide every adaptation.
questions.learningOutcome: Define equipment improvisation in sports and recreation.

questions.prompt: Which improvised item could safely mark a running lane during practice?
options: Soft cones made from visible plastic markers placed away from foot landing zones
Broken glass bottles placed on the track
Sharp metal rods hidden in the grass
Loose stones scattered across the lane
questions.correctAnswer: Soft cones made from visible plastic markers placed away from foot landing zones
questions.explanation: Improvised markers must be visible and safe if contacted. Sharp or hidden objects create avoidable injury risks.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify safe improvised equipment for athletics practice.

questions.prompt: Why should improvised equipment be tested before learners use it?
options: To confirm that it is safe, stable, and fit for the activity
To make learners wait without reason
To prove standard equipment is never useful
To avoid explaining the activity
questions.correctAnswer: To confirm that it is safe, stable, and fit for the activity
questions.explanation: Testing checks whether equipment can handle the intended use. It helps prevent failures that could injure learners.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain safety checks for improvised sports equipment.

questions.prompt: A school lacks relay batons for practice. Which solution is most appropriate?
options: Use smooth lightweight tubes of similar size after checking for sharp edges
Use heavy stones to make runners stronger
Use pointed sticks from a fence
Skip exchange practice for the whole term
questions.correctAnswer: Use smooth lightweight tubes of similar size after checking for sharp edges
questions.explanation: Relay practice needs safe objects that can be passed easily. Similar size helps learners practise realistic exchange technique.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply improvisation skills to solve equipment shortages in athletics.

questions.prompt: Which factor should guide the size of an improvised target for throwing practice?
options: Learner ability, skill objective, safety distance, and available space
Only the coach's favourite colour
The number of spectators expected
The price of a professional scoreboard
questions.correctAnswer: Learner ability, skill objective, safety distance, and available space
questions.explanation: Equipment should match the learning goal and learner level. Safety distance and space prevent collisions and stray throws.
questions.learningOutcome: Select equipment dimensions based on learning and safety needs.

questions.prompt: Which action best links equipment improvisation with environmental conservation?
options: Reuse clean safe materials such as plastic containers while avoiding harmful waste
Burn used plastic near the playing field
Cut live trees for every practice session
Throw damaged equipment into drainage channels
questions.correctAnswer: Reuse clean safe materials such as plastic containers while avoiding harmful waste
questions.explanation: Responsible improvisation can reduce waste by reusing safe materials. It should never create pollution or unsafe objects.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply environmental responsibility when improvising sports equipment.

questions.prompt: A learner proposes using water-filled glass bottles as training weights. What is the best analysis?
options: The idea is unsafe because glass can break and cut learners
It is best because heavier objects are always safer
It is acceptable only if learners lift faster
It removes the need for teacher supervision
questions.correctAnswer: The idea is unsafe because glass can break and cut learners
questions.explanation: Improvised equipment must not create new hazards. Plastic containers or other safer materials are better choices when appropriate.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse safety risks in proposed improvised equipment.

questions.prompt: Which design brief is best for learners making improvised agility markers?
options: Markers must be visible, lightweight, stable, reusable, and safe if stepped on
Markers must be sharp, heavy, hidden, and difficult to remove
Markers should block the whole field permanently
Markers should be made only if standard cones are available
questions.correctAnswer: Markers must be visible, lightweight, stable, reusable, and safe if stepped on
questions.explanation: A good design brief states the function and safety requirements. Agility markers should guide movement without causing injury.
questions.learningOutcome: Create criteria for designing safe improvised sports equipment.

questions.prompt: In athletics, what is a technical skill?
options: A specific movement technique used to perform an event effectively
A meeting held after a tournament
A list of school clubs
A financial record for equipment purchases
questions.correctAnswer: A specific movement technique used to perform an event effectively
questions.explanation: Technical skills are movement techniques such as sprint start, baton exchange, take-off, or throwing action. They affect performance quality.
questions.learningOutcome: Define technical skill in athletics.

questions.prompt: Which example shows a tactical decision in a middle-distance race?
options: Choosing when to increase pace before the finish
Tying shoelaces before the warm-up
Counting the number of cones in the store
Drawing the school badge on a vest
questions.correctAnswer: Choosing when to increase pace before the finish
questions.explanation: Tactical skills involve decisions that improve performance in context. Pacing and timing a finishing kick are tactical choices.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise tactical decisions in athletics events.

questions.prompt: Why is arm action important in sprinting technique?
options: It helps balance the body and supports rhythm and drive
It replaces the need for leg movement
It is used only to signal officials
It makes the track shorter
questions.correctAnswer: It helps balance the body and supports rhythm and drive
questions.explanation: Coordinated arm action supports sprint mechanics and balance. It works with leg drive rather than replacing it.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the function of arm action in sprinting.

questions.prompt: A relay team keeps slowing down during baton exchange. Which technical focus is most useful?
options: Practise exchange zone timing, hand position, and verbal cues
Train only long-distance jogging for the exchange
Hold the baton with both hands while running
Stop running before every handover
questions.correctAnswer: Practise exchange zone timing, hand position, and verbal cues
questions.explanation: Relay exchange depends on timing, target hand position, and communication. These technical details reduce speed loss.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply technical corrections to improve relay exchange performance.

questions.prompt: Which tactical plan suits a learner running a 1500 metre race for the first time?
options: Start at a controlled pace, maintain rhythm, then increase effort near the finish if able
Sprint all-out from the first step regardless of fitness
Stop every lap to check the crowd
Run in the outside lane for the entire race to cover more distance
questions.correctAnswer: Start at a controlled pace, maintain rhythm, then increase effort near the finish if able
questions.explanation: Middle-distance races require energy management. Controlled pacing helps prevent early fatigue.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply pacing tactics to middle-distance running.

questions.prompt: Which coaching cue best improves long jump take-off technique?
options: Drive the knee up and take off from the board with a tall body position
Look backward during take-off
Slow down completely before reaching the board
Land on the take-off foot only
questions.correctAnswer: Drive the knee up and take off from the board with a tall body position
questions.explanation: Effective take-off converts approach speed into lift. Knee drive and tall posture support better flight.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply technical cues for jumping events in athletics.

questions.prompt: A runner starts very fast but fades badly in the final 200 metres of a 400 metre race. What is the best tactical analysis?
options: The athlete may need better pace distribution and speed endurance
The athlete should ignore pacing and start even faster
The problem is only the colour of the lane
The final bend should be skipped during practice
questions.correctAnswer: The athlete may need better pace distribution and speed endurance
questions.explanation: A 400 metre race requires controlled speed and endurance. Going out too fast can cause severe fatigue before the finish.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse tactical pacing problems in athletics performance.

questions.prompt: Which training task best helps learners connect technique and tactics in athletics?
options: Run timed intervals while practising target pace and reviewing split times
Read event names without movement
Choose lane numbers randomly and avoid feedback
Practise only celebrations after races
questions.correctAnswer: Run timed intervals while practising target pace and reviewing split times
questions.explanation: Timed intervals develop technique, pacing, and data-based reflection. Reviewing split times helps learners adjust tactics.
questions.learningOutcome: Design an athletics task that combines technical execution and tactical decision-making.

questions.prompt: What is body conditioning in athletics?
options: Planned exercises that prepare the body for event demands
Painting lane markings before a race
Naming athletes during assembly
Choosing the colour of medals
questions.correctAnswer: Planned exercises that prepare the body for event demands
questions.explanation: Body conditioning develops fitness qualities needed in sport. It can include strength, endurance, mobility, balance, and speed work.
questions.learningOutcome: Define body conditioning for athletics performance.

questions.prompt: Which conditioning component is most important for a marathon runner?
options: Aerobic endurance
Maximum single jump height only
Hand-eye coordination only
Short-term memory only
questions.correctAnswer: Aerobic endurance
questions.explanation: Long-distance running depends heavily on sustained oxygen delivery and efficient energy use. Aerobic endurance is therefore central.
questions.learningOutcome: Match conditioning components to athletics event demands.

questions.prompt: Why should conditioning activities progress gradually?
options: Gradual progression allows the body to adapt and lowers injury risk
It guarantees that learners never get tired
It removes the need for technique practice
It makes all events require the same fitness
questions.correctAnswer: Gradual progression allows the body to adapt and lowers injury risk
questions.explanation: The body adapts to training over time. Sudden large increases in load can cause injury or excessive fatigue.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain progressive overload in body conditioning.

questions.prompt: Which conditioning activity best supports explosive power for jumping events?
options: Controlled bounding and jump drills after a proper warm-up
Long static sitting before take-off practice
Slow copying of rules into notebooks
Standing still until the session ends
questions.correctAnswer: Controlled bounding and jump drills after a proper warm-up
questions.explanation: Jumping events need explosive leg power. Bounding drills can develop this quality when taught safely and progressively.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply conditioning exercises to jumping event performance.

questions.prompt: A sprinter needs faster acceleration over the first 30 metres. Which conditioning focus is most useful?
options: Short resisted starts, leg power, and reaction drills
Only long slow walks
Only static stretching during the whole session
Avoiding all starting practice
questions.correctAnswer: Short resisted starts, leg power, and reaction drills
questions.explanation: Acceleration depends on power, start mechanics, and reaction. Short focused drills match the demand of the first metres.
questions.learningOutcome: Select conditioning drills for sprint acceleration.

questions.prompt: Which recovery practice should follow a hard athletics conditioning session?
options: Cool down, hydrate, stretch gently, and allow enough rest before the next hard session
Immediately repeat the session at higher intensity
Avoid drinking water until the next day
Ignore muscle soreness and keep sprinting
questions.correctAnswer: Cool down, hydrate, stretch gently, and allow enough rest before the next hard session
questions.explanation: Recovery helps the body adapt and reduces risk of excessive fatigue. Hydration, cool-down, and rest are practical recovery steps.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply recovery principles after conditioning activities.

questions.prompt: Two athletes follow the same conditioning plan, but one develops repeated knee pain. What should the coach analyse first?
options: Training load, technique, footwear, surface, and recovery
Only the athlete's favourite event
The colour of the stopwatch
Whether the athlete can shout team slogans
questions.correctAnswer: Training load, technique, footwear, surface, and recovery
questions.explanation: Repeated pain can come from load, movement quality, equipment, surface, or insufficient recovery. A coach should review these factors before progressing.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse factors that affect safety in conditioning programmes.

questions.prompt: Which conditioning plan best prepares a school athletics squad with sprinters, jumpers, and distance runners?
options: General warm-up and mobility, then event-specific groups for speed, power, or endurance, followed by cool-down
One identical maximum sprint session for every athlete every day
Only distance running for all athletes regardless of event
No conditioning because technical skill is the only factor
questions.correctAnswer: General warm-up and mobility, then event-specific groups for speed, power, or endurance, followed by cool-down
questions.explanation: Different athletics events require different conditioning emphasis. A shared warm-up plus event-specific work supports both safety and performance.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a differentiated conditioning session for varied athletics events.

questions.prompt: What is talent identification in sports?
options: Recognising learners with potential for further development in a sport
Selecting only the oldest learners for every team
Choosing players by friendship groups
Awarding medals before any activity starts
questions.correctAnswer: Recognising learners with potential for further development in a sport
questions.explanation: Talent identification looks for potential using evidence from performance, learning ability, attitude, and physical qualities. It should be fair and systematic.
questions.learningOutcome: Define talent identification in sports and recreation.

questions.prompt: Which evidence is most useful when identifying potential in athletics?
options: Repeated performance results, technique, attitude, and improvement over time
Only the learner's popularity in class
Only the colour of the learner's shoes
A single lucky performance with no follow-up
questions.correctAnswer: Repeated performance results, technique, attitude, and improvement over time
questions.explanation: Talent decisions should use more than one observation. Consistent data and growth over time give fairer evidence.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify evidence used in fair talent detection.

questions.prompt: Why should coaches avoid selecting talent based on body size alone?
options: Skill, attitude, coordination, learning rate, and maturation also affect potential
Body size is always the only predictor of success
Smaller learners cannot improve in any sport
Larger learners never need coaching
questions.correctAnswer: Skill, attitude, coordination, learning rate, and maturation also affect potential
questions.explanation: Talent is multidimensional. Fair selection considers both current ability and future development potential.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the need for multiple criteria in talent identification.

questions.prompt: A learner has average speed but learns technique quickly and trains consistently. What should the coach do?
options: Continue monitoring and provide development opportunities
Remove the learner because speed is the only talent measure
Ignore attendance and effort
Select only learners who already perform perfectly
questions.correctAnswer: Continue monitoring and provide development opportunities
questions.explanation: Rapid learning and consistency are useful indicators of potential. Development opportunities can reveal talent over time.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply talent identification criteria beyond immediate performance.

questions.prompt: Which method best supports fair talent detection during inter-class games?
options: Use common criteria, observe all learners, and record evidence over several activities
Ask only team captains to choose their friends
Select the first learners who arrive at the field
Avoid recording performance information
questions.correctAnswer: Use common criteria, observe all learners, and record evidence over several activities
questions.explanation: Fair detection needs transparent criteria and repeated observation. Records reduce bias and help track progress.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply fair procedures for school-level talent identification.

questions.prompt: Which action best supports a talented learner's long-term development?
options: Provide progressive training, feedback, rest, education support, and competition exposure
Push the learner into hard competition every day
Ignore schoolwork because sport is enough
Stop coaching once the learner wins one race
questions.correctAnswer: Provide progressive training, feedback, rest, education support, and competition exposure
questions.explanation: Talent development is long-term and balanced. Training, recovery, feedback, and education all support sustainable growth.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply development support for learners with sports potential.

questions.prompt: A school trial selects only learners who can afford private sports shoes. What is the main weakness of this process?
options: It introduces unfair resource bias into talent identification
It measures all talent dimensions accurately
It guarantees the best long-term athletes
It removes the need for observation
questions.correctAnswer: It introduces unfair resource bias into talent identification
questions.explanation: Selection should not depend on family resources. Fair processes use accessible activities and evidence-based criteria.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse bias and equity issues in talent identification.

questions.prompt: Which talent development record would be most useful for a coach over one term?
options: Performance tests, attendance, technical notes, feedback, goals, and progress reflections
Only a list of nicknames
Only the final score of one friendly match
A blank notebook kept away from training
questions.correctAnswer: Performance tests, attendance, technical notes, feedback, goals, and progress reflections
questions.explanation: A development record should show evidence of growth and learning needs. It helps coaches plan next steps for each learner.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a simple record for monitoring sports talent development.

questions.prompt: What is officiating in sport?
options: Applying rules to guide fair and safe competition
Training only the winning team after a match
Selling tickets at the gate
Choosing school uniforms for athletes
questions.correctAnswer: Applying rules to guide fair and safe competition
questions.explanation: Officials use rules to manage play, protect safety, and support fairness. Their decisions help competitions run properly.
questions.learningOutcome: Define officiating and its purpose in sport.

questions.prompt: Which principle should guide an official's decision during a disputed call?
options: Impartiality based on rules and observed evidence
Favouring the home team
Changing the decision to please spectators
Guessing without watching the action
questions.correctAnswer: Impartiality based on rules and observed evidence
questions.explanation: Good officiating requires fairness and rule-based judgement. Officials should not be influenced by pressure or personal preference.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain impartiality as a principle of officiating.

questions.prompt: A referee notices unsafe tackles increasing in a football match. What should the referee do?
options: Enforce the rules promptly to protect players and control the match
Ignore the tackles so the game remains fast
Ask spectators to decide every foul
Stop using the whistle for the rest of the match
questions.correctAnswer: Enforce the rules promptly to protect players and control the match
questions.explanation: Officials have a duty to protect player safety and fairness. Timely enforcement discourages dangerous play.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply officiating principles to maintain safety and fairness.

questions.prompt: Which action shows good communication by an official?
options: Use clear signals, calm voice, and brief explanations when needed
Shout insults at players
Hide decisions from teams
Use different signals for the same rule every time
questions.correctAnswer: Use clear signals, calm voice, and brief explanations when needed
questions.explanation: Clear communication helps players understand decisions and continue safely. Consistent signals reduce confusion.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply effective communication during officiating.

questions.prompt: An official is technically correct but speaks rudely to players. What is the best evaluation?
options: Rule knowledge is useful, but poor communication can reduce respect and match control
Rudeness improves fairness
Communication is unrelated to officiating
Players should never hear any official's decision
questions.correctAnswer: Rule knowledge is useful, but poor communication can reduce respect and match control
questions.explanation: Officials need both rule knowledge and professional conduct. Respectful communication supports authority and cooperation.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how conduct affects officiating effectiveness.

questions.prompt: Which checklist best prepares a learner to officiate a school game?
options: Know rules, inspect equipment and area, confirm roles, use signals, stay impartial, and record incidents
Arrive late, guess rules, and avoid signals
Let players decide every rule during disputes
Focus only on the final score and ignore safety
questions.correctAnswer: Know rules, inspect equipment and area, confirm roles, use signals, stay impartial, and record incidents
questions.explanation: Preparation helps officials manage safety, fairness, communication, and records. A checklist supports consistent performance.
questions.learningOutcome: Create an officiating preparation checklist for school sport.

questions.prompt: Who is a meet official in athletics?
options: An official who helps organise and judge events during an athletics meeting
A player who competes in every race
A spectator who cheers loudly
A coach who replaces all judges
questions.correctAnswer: An official who helps organise and judge events during an athletics meeting
questions.explanation: Meet officials support the running of athletics competitions. Their roles can include judging, timing, measuring, recording, or marshalling.
questions.subStrandTitle: Responsibilities of Technical and Meet Officials
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the role of meet officials in athletics.

questions.prompt: Which duty is most likely performed by a timekeeper in a track event?
options: Measuring and recording athletes' finishing times accurately
Preparing lunch for all spectators
Choosing team slogans
Changing the event rules after each heat
questions.correctAnswer: Measuring and recording athletes' finishing times accurately
questions.explanation: A timekeeper records performance times according to competition procedures. Accurate timing supports fair results.
questions.subStrandTitle: Responsibilities of Technical and Meet Officials
questions.learningOutcome: Explain duties of technical officials in athletics events.

questions.prompt: A long jump judge sees that a learner steps beyond the take-off board. What should the judge do?
options: Record the attempt as a foul according to the event rules
Measure the jump as if the take-off was legal
Ask the crowd whether to allow it
Move the board after the jump to hide the fault
questions.correctAnswer: Record the attempt as a foul according to the event rules
questions.explanation: Technical officials apply event rules consistently. A foul at take-off cannot be measured as a valid jump.
questions.subStrandTitle: Responsibilities of Technical and Meet Officials
questions.learningOutcome: Apply technical official duties during field events.

questions.prompt: Why is accurate record keeping important during a school athletics meet?
options: It supports fair ranking, progress tracking, and resolution of disputes
It makes warm-ups unnecessary
It allows officials to ignore measurements
It ensures every athlete receives the same result
questions.correctAnswer: It supports fair ranking, progress tracking, and resolution of disputes
questions.explanation: Records provide evidence for results and later review. Accurate recording helps protect fairness and transparency.
questions.subStrandTitle: Responsibilities of Technical and Meet Officials
questions.learningOutcome: Apply accurate recording practices during sports events.

questions.prompt: During a crowded school meet, athletes miss calls for their events. Which official responsibility needs improvement?
options: Marshalling and communication of event schedules
Designing new team uniforms
Changing race distances without notice
Selecting only popular athletes
questions.correctAnswer: Marshalling and communication of event schedules
questions.explanation: Marshalling helps athletes report to the right place at the right time. Clear communication keeps events organised and fair.
questions.subStrandTitle: Responsibilities of Technical and Meet Officials
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse organisational problems in event officiating.

questions.prompt: Which staffing plan best supports fair and safe officiating at an inter-house athletics meet?
options: Assign trained starters, timekeepers, judges, recorders, marshals, and first-aid support with clear duties
Use one untrained official for all events and records
Let athletes measure their own results without supervision
Run all events without safety checks or role allocation
questions.correctAnswer: Assign trained starters, timekeepers, judges, recorders, marshals, and first-aid support with clear duties
questions.explanation: A meet needs clear roles so events run safely and fairly. Trained officials and first-aid support reduce confusion and risk.
questions.subStrandTitle: Responsibilities of Technical and Meet Officials
questions.learningOutcome: Create an officiating role allocation plan for a school athletics meet.
